pageTitle: History & Architecture — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: History & architecture
text: History & architecture Almost a thousand years of building, one century's alteration at a time — right up to a contemporary extension finished in 2007.

pageTitle: History & Architecture — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: A church built in layers
text: A church built in layers The earliest parts of St Martin of Tours date from the 12th century, and the church is mentioned in the Textus Roffensis, dated 1122 — so it is almost a thousand years old. Like most medieval parish churches, it wasn't built all at once — each generation added or altered what it needed: 12th century The earliest parts of the church building. 13th century The tower and a chapel were added. 15th century A porch was built. 19th century A clergy vestry was added. 2007 The Br

pageTitle: History & Architecture — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: The Brass Crosby Room
text: The Brass Crosby Room Rather than imitate the medieval building, the 2007 extension — designed by Clague Architects — was built as a clearly contemporary "north aisle," linked to the existing church at the west end of the nave and through the tower. The design was scaled deliberately subordinate to the historic nave, borrowing its proportions and materials, while still reading unmistakably as a modern addition rather than a pastiche. It was developed with the Diocesan Advisory Committee and the

pageTitle: History & Architecture — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: Inside the church
text: Inside the church The earliest dateable parts of the church are in the Early English style, characterised by the triple lancet windows at the east end. The glass in them has been replaced many times. The current windows were designed by Moira Forsythe in the early 1950s, replacing the Victorian glass destroyed by the blast from a flying bomb during the 1939–45 war. She also made the small window of St John in St John's Chapel. The tower and tower arch were added in the 13th century. The wooden s

pageTitle: History & Architecture — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: Brass Crosby
text: Brass Crosby The Brass Crosby Room is named after Brass Crosby, who was Lord of the Manor of Chelsfield and Lord Mayor of London, and a champion of the liberty of the press. In the late 1700s he was imprisoned in the Tower of London after demanding that the minutes of Parliament be published; public support led to his release. Tradition links him with the saying "as bold as brass". A memorial to Brass Crosby is on the north wall of the aisle of the church, and a Blue Plaque is on a post to the l

pageTitle: History & Architecture — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: The parish of Chelsfield
text: The parish of Chelsfield Chelsfield stands on high ground to the east of Orpington, only 16 miles from London, and has always been popular with people from London who come to visit, walk and live. The name probably comes from Saxon times and means "a cold place". The chief manor houses were Woodlands, Chelsfield House, Hewitts and Court Lodge, next to the church. As in most English villages, the squires and the Lord of the Manor set up the system of land use and provided work for local people. C

pageTitle: History & Architecture — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: Well Hill Mission
text: Well Hill Mission Well Hill Mission Chapel was built in 1893 on land donated by the Hart-Dyke family of Lullingstone Castle. It was originally part of the Parish of Shoreham, and was one of three mission chapels built for the growing number of hop and fruit pickers. Boundary changes in the middle of the 20th century transferred it to the Parish of Chelsfield. pageTitle: History & Architecture — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: Our Benefice
text: Our Benefice St Martin's is part of the Benefice of Chelsfield with Green St Green and Pratts Bottom. The proposal for a joint Benefice was approved in November 2019, and from 1 June 2021 St Martin's became part of it, with Revd Susan Atkinson-Jones as its Rector. Our neighbours at St Mary's, Green Street Green have their own website: www.smasch.org. St Martin's is listed on the Small Pilgrim Places Network, and is a corporate member of the Prayer Book Society.

pageTitle: Churchyard — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: A peaceful haven
text: A peaceful haven Our churchyard is about four acres, and it is a peaceful haven. It has been a sought-after resting place for parishioners for hundreds of years. The names on the war memorial in the porch, and the scattering of war graves, are remembered each year on Remembrance Sunday. Different areas reflect the season: there are drifts of snowdrops in January; daffodils, primroses, cowslips and ladies smock in March; a sea of cow-parsley in June; and a well-kept lawn for summer weddings. In t

pageTitle: Churchyard — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: Looking after the churchyard
text: Looking after the churchyard All of this takes a great deal of upkeep. A contractor looks after the grounds in the summer, and we rely on volunteers for the rest: cutting the lawn used for weddings, keeping the paths and grass in order (with care, so that the wild flowers and wildlife are protected), and joining special clearance days for the tougher jobs. pageTitle: Setting Up Your Laptop — Help — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: 1. Install Claude Desktop
text: 1. Install Claude Desktop Download it from claude.com/download and sign in (or create an account).

pageTitle: Setting Up Your Laptop — Help — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: 2. Create a GitHub account
text: 2. Create a GitHub account This site's source code lives on GitHub. Create a free account at github.com/join if you don't already have one. Before you request access, turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) on your new account: in GitHub, go to Settings → Password and authentication → Two-factor authentication and follow the setup steps (an authenticator app is the easiest option). pageTitle: Making a Change — Help — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: Making a change
text: Making a change What happens, step by step, when you ask Claude to update the site.

pageTitle: Making a Change — Help — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: Just describe what you want changed
text: Just describe what you want changed Open Claude Desktop in this project and describe the change in plain English — "update the Wednesday service time to 10am" or "add a new photo to the About page." Claude edits the right source file, rebuilds the site, and shows you the result.

pageTitle: Making a Change — Help — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: What Claude checks before anything goes live
text: What Claude checks before anything goes live Every change runs through the same checks: the automated test suite (including an accessibility scan of every page), a dependency security check, and a rebuild that regenerates every page from its source. Nothing is pushed live until those pass.

pageTitle: Making a Change — Help — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: Where each fact lives
text: Where each fact lives Each kind of fact is kept in one place, so one change updates every page that uses it. You don't need to open these files, but naming the right one helps Claude make the right change. People The clergy and officers on Clergy & contacts, with their photos, are in people.config.mjs. Services & events The calendar is in events.config.mjs. Address & phone The church address, the Rectory phone number and the parish email are in site.config.mjs. Gallery photos Added in gallery.co

pageTitle: Making a Change — Help — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: Common questions
text: Common questions Can I break it? Not permanently — every change is a new, separate save point. See When It Goes Wrong. Do I need to know code? No — describe what you want in plain English. How long until it's live? Once pushed, Cloudflare deploys automatically, usually within a minute or two.

pageTitle: Technical Details — Help — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: Technical details
text: Technical details The real infrastructure behind this site, for anyone who wants it.

pageTitle: Technical Details — Help — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: Hosting
text: Hosting Built to deploy to Cloudflare Workers, the same platform used for other MediaWright-built parish sites — but not yet live, and not yet pointed at a domain. See "About this build" in the repository's CLAUDE.md for why.

pageTitle: Technical Details — Help — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: The templated build
text: The templated build Every page in public/ is generated from templates/ and src/pages/ by scripts/build.mjs — never hand-edited directly. This keeps the header, footer, contact details and safeguarding information consistent across every page from one source.

pageTitle: Technical Details — Help — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: Testing
text: Testing Every page is scanned for accessibility issues with axe-core, and a Playwright test suite checks navigation, forms, the calendar, and search. npm audit checks for known vulnerabilities in dependencies. All of this runs before every push.

pageTitle: Technical Details — Help — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: Newsletter signup
text: Newsletter signup The signup form posts to a Cloudflare Worker endpoint that talks to MailerLite — but no MailerLite account has been connected yet (see wrangler.jsonc's placeholder group id). The form and its tests work end-to-end; a real signup won't until that's configured.

pageTitle: When It Goes Wrong — Help — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: When something goes wrong
text: When something goes wrong Nothing here is ever permanently broken.

pageTitle: When It Goes Wrong — Help — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: A change looks wrong
text: A change looks wrong Just tell Claude what looks off — "the phone number in the footer is wrong now" — and ask it to fix or revert that specific change.

pageTitle: When It Goes Wrong — Help — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: Revert to how things were
text: Revert to how things were Every change is its own save point in the site's history. Ask Claude to "undo the last change" or "go back to how the Contact page looked before," and it can restore exactly that.

pageTitle: When It Goes Wrong — Help — St Martin of Tours, Chelsfield
heading: Still stuck?
text: Still stuck? Contact whoever manages this repository (see Technical Details) — nothing is unrecoverable, so there's no need to panic.
